title: Soft gradients in a recording come out smooth, even where the Mac draws them in steps
goal: Recordings still show visible bands across soft dark gradients, such as a translucent terminal window. The recording now copies the screen exactly, and the screen's own pixels are in steps, so Photonz has to smooth those steps into the finer shades its recordings can hold, without blurring text or edges and without slowing recording down.
notes:
User, 2026-11-16, after a-screen-recording-keeps-the-desktop-s-colours-a shipped (ce7a9b934, 10-bit HEVC Display P3, captured as kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr10BiPlanarVideoRange in ScreenRecorder.swift:304): "there is no way to fix the visible banding in the recordings? see last recording", with Screenshot 2026-11-16 at 06.33.51.png (the recording playing in Photonz Dev).

Measured by the intake window, G channel down a 1300 px column of the empty sidebar (x 261, y 740..2040): the macOS screenshot of the screen (06.33.18, before the recording) has 11 levels over 53..63, 16 changes, longest flat run 164 px, max step 1. The recording's frame at 3 s, decoded to 16 bit: 8-bit equivalent 11 levels, longest run 161 px; in 10-bit, 28 levels, longest run 116 px, steps of about 3.5 to 4 codes = one 8-bit shade. Colours match within about 1 code. So the recording is now faithful; the SOURCE is drawn in 8-bit steps by the window server (the window's translucent material), and capturing at 10 bit cannot add shades that were never drawn. Whether the user's display hides those steps (panel dithering) is not confirmed; the user sees them as bands in the recording.

ffmpeg deband test on that frame (format=yuv420p10le, deband=1thr=0.004:2thr=0.004:3thr=0.004:range=64:blur=1): 43 levels, longest flat run 35 px. gradfun (8-bit) did not help (10 levels). ffmpeg's CPU deband took 0.6 s wall for 30 frames on 5 cores, far too heavy for 60 fps live, hence the GPU requirement. Smoothing in the player and export instead of at capture keeps recording cheap and the file a faithful copy; smoothing at capture fixes the file for every other player. Measure both. The Smaller files quality setting (Settings > Recording > Quality) must get the same pass.
acceptance: Reproduced first on the user's own files: /Users/dzearing/Pictures/Screenshots/Recording 2026-11-16 at 06.33.31.mp4 at 3 s against Screenshot 2026-11-16 at 06.33.18.png, the empty sidebar strip of the Ghoztty window (x 260, y 740 to 2040). Measure what the intake window measured (below) and put it in the audit

A smoothing pass (a deband: where neighbouring areas differ by about one 8-bit shade over a wide flat run, blend them into a smooth 10-bit ramp; leave anything with a real edge alone) is applied to recordings, run on the GPU (Metal / Core Image), not the CPU. The audit says where it runs (as frames are captured, or when a recording is played and exported) and why, MEASURED

Visual bar that today's file FAILS: on that strip the longest flat run is under 40 px and there are at least 35 distinct 10-bit levels (today: 116 px and 28 levels; ffmpeg's deband filter on the same frame reached 35 px and 43 levels, so it can be done). Same bar on a controlled test: a full-screen 8-bit gradient spanning 10 shades over 1300 px

Nothing sharp gets softer: text, window edges, icons and one-pixel lines in the same frames differ from the unsmoothed frame by no more than 1 10-bit code value at the 99th percentile (measured on a text-heavy crop), and colours stay within Delta E 1 of the screenshot

Recording stays light and quick: start latency, dropped frames over a minute at 60 fps, and the CPU and GPU it adds are measured before and after; none gets worse by more than 10 percent. File size per minute before and after is listed

Played in QuickTime and in Photonz's player, the before and after crops are put side by side (and a 3x enlarged, contrast-stretched crop so the bands can be seen) under queue/audits/, with a short before/after clip of the user's recording, named in the audit; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not
